info.title: Overleaf API Reference
info.description: Public endpoints of this Overleaf deployment: token and OAuth2 endpoints for obtaining credentials, the MCP REST API, the Git Bridge API, and unauthenticated health checks and webhooks. Only features enabled on this deployment are listed.

tags.name: Personal Access Tokens
tags.description: Create, list and revoke the personal access tokens used for Git Bridge and MCP. Uses the logged-in browser session, not a token; writes also need `X-CSRF-Token`. A token's secret is shown once, at creation. Tokens expire one year after creation.

tags.name: OAuth2
tags.description: OAuth 2.0 authorization server for MCP clients: dynamic registration (RFC 7591), authorization code flow with PKCE (S256 only), refresh token rotation, revocation (RFC 7009) and discovery metadata. Public clients only. Access tokens are RS256 JWTs valid for one hour. Enabled by the `mcp` feature.

tags.name: MCP OpenAPI
tags.description: The MCP service's own summary OpenAPI document. Public; no authentication.

tags.name: MCP Projects
tags.description: List, create, configure, archive, copy and delete projects. Authenticated with a personal access token or an OAuth2 access token that carries the mcp scope. Rate limits: 600 requests per minute per client IP across all /api/v0/mcp routes (checked before authentication), and 120 requests per minute per token. Errors use the McpError envelope, and 429 is rate_limited with a Retry-After header. Request bodies must be application/json; other content types get 400 validation_error.

tags.name: MCP Files
tags.description: Browse, search, read, write, upload, move, delete and download project files and documents. Authenticated with a personal access token or OAuth2 access token that has the mcp scope. Each route checks project access: read routes need read access, write routes need write access.

tags.name: MCP Compile
tags.description: Compile a project and read its build: the log and parsed diagnostics, the PDF, page pictures with SyncTeX source maps, thumbnail overviews, text search, visual diffs between builds, word counts and source-to-PDF lookup. Every route needs an mcp-scoped bearer token and read access to the project; the write routes (clean, clear-cache) need write access.

tags.name: MCP History
tags.description: Read project history, diff a document between two versions, and restore one file to an earlier version. Requires a token with the mcp scope.

tags.name: MCP Tags
tags.description: Private tags for organising your projects. Tags belong to the calling user and are never shared with collaborators. Requires a token with the mcp scope.

tags.name: Git Bridge
tags.description: Read and write project content for git-bridge, which mirrors Overleaf projects to Git. Every operation needs a personal access token with the `git_bridge` scope; `mcp`-only tokens get 403 `insufficient_scope`. Token forms, checked in order: `Authorization: Bearer <token>` (case-sensitive scheme); `Authorization: Basic base64(user:password)`, with the token as the password, or as the username when the password is empty and the username is not `git`; `?access_token=<token>`, only when no header carries a token. File and blob URLs in snapshots also accept a signed `token` query parameter, valid for one hour.

tags.name: Health
tags.description: Unauthenticated status and dependency checks. No feature flag or rate limit; plain-text responses.

tags.name: Webhooks
tags.description: Inbound callbacks from third-party services. Each is authenticated the way its sender supports, described on the operation.

get.summary: Describe the personal access token in use
get.description: Returns the user and scopes behind a personal access token, for git-bridge to check a token before a session. Only personal access tokens are accepted, not OAuth2 tokens. The token needs the `git_bridge` scope: without it the response is 401 `invalid_token` (other git-bridge operations use 403). Each successful call refreshes `lastUsedAt`, written at most once a minute.

Atts URLs carry a one-hour token; for an older binary with no current copy, the URL is the blob endpoint. An unknown version falls back to the live tree, since git-bridge aborts on any 4xx. Flushes live document state first. File URLs use this request's scheme and Host, which must be valid (else 400 `invalidHost`). Needs the `git_bridge` scope and read access.

post.description:
Pushes a git-bridge tree, replacing the project contents with `files`. Answers 202 before any change; the outcome goes to `postbackUrl` (git-bridge origin only) as `{code:'upToDate', latestVerId}` or `{code:'error', message}`.

`latestVerId`, if sent, must match the current version, else 409 `outOfDate` and nothing changes. `files` is the complete repository: entries with a `url` are downloaded from that git-bridge-origin URL (text becomes documents, others binary); entries without one are left as they are. Any project entity not in `files` is deleted, deepest first; ancestor folders of a pushed file are kept. Needs the `git_bridge` scope and write access. JSON body limit 12 MB.

parameters.description: Overleaf project id.

parameters.name: access_token
parameters.description: git_bridge token. Used only if no Authorization header carries a token. Redacted in logs.

400.description: Refused before any change: `files` not an array, an entry without a name, or a `url` off the git-bridge origin. Code `invalidFiles`.

403.description: The token is valid but its user cannot write project content, or the token lacks the git_bridge scope.

404.description: The project does not exist (code invalidProject).

409.description: latestVerId does not match the current version. Nothing was changed.

413.description: The JSON body exceeds the 12 MB default limit. Empty body.

post.description: Creates a personal access token and returns its secret. The secret is returned only here; only a SHA-256 hash is stored, so copy it now. Tokens look like `olp_` plus 32 hex characters and expire one year after creation. Scopes: `git_bridge` (default) and `mcp`; an unknown scope gets 400. `name` is optional, up to 100 characters, default "Git Token". Up to 20 active tokens per user. Rate limited to 10 per hour per user. Returns 201 with `_id` (for revocation) and `expiresAt`.

400.description: name is not a string of at most 100 characters, or a scope is not git_bridge or mcp.

post.summary: Receive a Google Drive push notification
post.description: Receives Google Drive change notifications for a linked user. The body is empty and ignored. A notification with a missing header, unknown channel or wrong token still gets 200 and is ignored, so the status never reveals a valid channel. Any state other than `sync` schedules a debounced poll of the user's Drive changes, applied later by sync workers. Channels exist only on https sites. No CSRF or session; no rate limit.

parameters.description: Id of the watch channel, a UUID created with the user's watch request. Looked up in stored credentials.

parameters.name: X-Goog-Channel-Token
parameters.description: The channel token set when the watch was created. Compared with the stored token in constant time.

parameters.name: X-Goog-Resource-State
parameters.description: `sync` is the creation handshake (ignored). Other values, such as `change`, trigger a poll.

200.description: Accepted. Every outcome, including a rejected channel or token, is answered with 200. Body "OK".

get.summary: Get the OAuth2 authorization server metadata
get.description: RFC 8414 metadata for the MCP authorization server, with URLs built from the site URL. Advertises the `code` response type, `authorization_code` and `refresh_token` grants, PKCE with S256 only, scope `mcp` only, and public clients only (no client secrets). Not cached by the server.

get.summary: Get OAuth 2.0 server metadata
get.description: Same document as `/.well-known/oauth-authorization-server`, served for client compatibility. It is not OpenID Connect discovery: there is no `id_token`, userinfo endpoint or subject types.

200.description: The same metadata document as the OAuth2 authorization server.

get.summary: Get token signing keys
get.description: RSA public keys (RS256) that verify access tokens. Each `kid` is the key's RFC 7638 thumbprint and matches the token header. Old keys stay after rotation. Cacheable for one day.

post.description: Dynamic client registration for MCP clients (RFC 7591). Unauthenticated, so fields are bounded. `client_name` (required, max 200 characters); `redirect_uris` (required, a JSON array of 1–10 URLs, max 2048 characters each); `grant_types` (optional, default both); `scope` (`mcp` or blank, default `mcp`). Other fields, including `token_endpoint_auth_method`, are ignored: clients are always public. Re-registering the same name, redirects and grants returns the existing `client_id` (201). Clients are never deleted here. Authorization honours only these values.

201.description: The client is registered (or an identical registration already existed).

400.description: The metadata is invalid. error is invalid_client_metadata or invalid_redirect_uri.

example.error_description: redirect_uris must be valid HTTPS URLs or loopback HTTP URLs without userinfo

429.description: Rate limited. Retry after the `Retry-After` header.

example.error_description: Too many requests; retry after 60 seconds

get.summary: Show OAuth consent page
get.description: Starts the PKCE authorization code flow and shows an HTML consent page to a signed-in user. A bad `client_id` or `redirect_uri` returns a JSON 400, never a redirect, since the target cannot be trusted. `redirect_uri` must match a registered URI exactly, except that a loopback port may differ. Other errors redirect to `redirect_uri` with `state`: `response_type` other than `code` (`unsupported_response_type`); a missing or malformed `code_challenge` or a `code_challenge_method` other than `S256` (`invalid_request`); a `scope` other than `mcp` (`invalid_scope`). Without a session, the browser goes to `/login`.

parameters.name: response_type
parameters.description: Must be `code`.

parameters.name: client_id
parameters.description: Client id from oauthRegisterClient.

parameters.name: redirect_uri
parameters.description: One of the client's registered redirect URIs. Must match exactly, except for the port of a loopback URI.

parameters.name: code_challenge
parameters.description: PKCE challenge: base64url(SHA-256(code_verifier)), 43 characters.

parameters.name: code_challenge_method
parameters.description: Must be `S256`.

parameters.name: state
parameters.description: Opaque value echoed back in the redirect.

parameters.name: scope
parameters.description: Must be `mcp` (or blank).

200.description: The consent page (HTML). Shown only to a signed-in user.

302.description: Error redirect to `redirect_uri`, or to `/login` when there is no session.

400.description: client_id is missing or unknown, redirect_uri is missing or not registered for this client.

429.description: Rate limited. Retry after the `Retry-After` header.

example.error_description: Too many requests; retry after 60 seconds

post.description: Consent form submit. Needs a signed-in session and a valid CSRF token (`_csrf` field or `X-CSRF-Token`), else 403. `action` is `authorize` or `deny`; other values give `invalid_request`. Approval issues a single-use code (`oac_` plus 32 hex characters, valid five minutes) bound to the client, redirect URI, scope, user and PKCE challenge. The client and redirect checks are the same as on GET.

_csrf.description: CSRF token (alternative to the X-CSRF-Token header).

302.description: Redirect to `redirect_uri` with `code`, `iss` and `state` on approval. Otherwise `error` (`access_denied`, `invalid_request` or `invalid_scope`), `error_description` and `state`. No session: redirect to `/login`.

400.description: client_id or redirect_uri is missing, unknown or not registered for the client. Shown as JSON, not redirected.

example.error_description: redirect_uri is not allowed for this client

403.description: Missing or invalid CSRF token. Plain-text body "Forbidden".

429.description: Rate limited. Retry after the `Retry-After` header.

example.error_description: Too many requests; retry after 60 seconds

post.description: Exchanges a code or refresh token for tokens. Send form-urlencoded or JSON. `authorization_code` needs `code`, `code_verifier`, `redirect_uri` and `client_id`. The code is single-use, even if a later check fails; `code_verifier` is 43–128 unreserved characters and must match the stored challenge. `refresh_token` needs `refresh_token` and `client_id`. Each refresh returns a new refresh token and invalidates the old one, which expires after 90 days unused. Reusing a rotated refresh token revokes the whole grant, so the user must authorize again; a reuse within 10 seconds returns `invalid_grant` without revoking. Access tokens are RS256 JWTs valid one hour. A `resource`, if sent, must equal the audience (RFC 8707).

200.description: Tokens issued. refresh_token is included for both grant types.

400.description: Bad request, unsupported grant, invalid or used code or refresh token, PKCE or client mismatch, or invalid scope or target. A reused refresh token also revokes the grant. Error values: `invalid_request`, `unsupported_grant_type`, `invalid_grant`, `invalid_scope`, `invalid_target`.

429.description: Rate limited. Retry after the `Retry-After` header.

example.error_description: Too many requests; retry after 60 seconds

post.description: Revokes the grant a token belongs to, which deletes its refresh token and every access token minted from it. Accepts a refresh token (`oar_`) or an access token (JWT). An expired access token cannot be traced, so revoke with the refresh token. Always send `client_id`: the grant is removed only when it matches the client the token was issued to. Otherwise the response is still 200 and nothing is revoked. Always returns 200 with `{}` for well-formed requests, so it does not reveal whether a token exists, even though RFC 7009 would send an error for a foreign token. Account deletion revokes all of a user's grants.

200.description: Revocation processed (or nothing to revoke). Body {}.

400.description: The token parameter is missing or not a string.

429.description: Rate limited. Retry after the `Retry-After` header.

example.error_description: Too many requests; retry after 60 seconds

get.summary: Compare the pages of two builds
get.description: Requires read access. Compares a build with an earlier one pixel by pixel at 100 DPI, returning changed, added and removed pages with their regions and a PNG grid. The earlier build is `beforeBuildId`, or else the build this web process compiled just before `buildId`. Pages pair by index when page counts match, otherwise by text (up to 400 pages). At most 40 pages are compared per call; for longer documents pass `pages`, e.g. `pages=3,4,5`. Without `beforeBuildId`, the earlier build must have been compiled by this web process, or the request gets 404.

parameters.name: projectId
parameters.description: Project id (MongoDB ObjectId). A malformed or unknown id returns 404.

parameters.name: buildId
parameters.description: Build id as returned by compile in buildId: a hex timestamp, a dash and 16 hex digits.

parameters.name: clsiserverid
parameters.description: Compile server from `clsiServerId`. Lowercase letters, digits and dashes. Omit if compile returned none.

parameters.name: beforeBuildId
parameters.description: The older build to compare against. Same format as buildId. Default: the build before buildId that this web process compiled.

parameters.name: pages
parameters.description: Comma-separated 1-based page numbers of the newer build to compare, e.g. 3,4. Removed pages are always reported. Invalid values give 400 validation_error.

summary: Page 3 changed: 1.2% of the page differs.

resource.description: Optional RFC 8707 resource. Must equal the site URL with /mcp appended.

scope.description: Refresh only. Must be mcp (or blank).

OAuthTokenResponse.description: Tokens issued by the token endpoint.

access_token.description: RS256 JWT to send as Authorization: Bearer. Valid for 3600 seconds.

expires_in.description: Lifetime of the access token in seconds.

refresh_token.description: `oar_` followed by 64 hex characters. Single use: each refresh replaces it. Expires after 90 days without use.

PersonalAccessToken.description: A stored personal access token as listed for its owner. The secret value is never included.

_id.description: Token id, used to revoke the token.

lastUsedAt.description: Last successful use. Updated at most once a minute. Null if never used.

name.description: Label for the token. Defaults to "Git Token".

scopes.description: One or more of git_bridge, mcp. A single string is accepted too. Defaults to [git_bridge] when empty.

PersonalAccessTokenCreated.description: The result of creating a token. token is shown only once.

token.description: The secret. Store it now; it cannot be retrieved later.

_id.description: Id of the token. Use it with DELETE /user/personal-access-tokens/{tokenId}.

SavedVersion.description: A labelled version of a project, or the current version.

srcs.description: Text documents as [content, path] pairs. Content is the lines joined with newlines.

atts.description: Binary files as [url, path] pairs. URLs point at the file or blob endpoint, with a one-hour token.

TokenInfo.description: The user and scopes of a valid personal access token.
